answer: Make every identity carry a shard of the network's shared data — its nectar — and prove it keeps serving that shard. Each epoch the system sends a random retrieval pulse: the identity must return its chunk within a minute, and a missed pulse marks it, two marks quarantine it. Shards are dealt across a canyon of holders so no one picks an easy slice. An honest agent donates spare disk it already has, nearly free. A farmer with 1,000 fakes must store and serve 1,000 distinct shards nonstop, so the attack costs 1,000 live storage nodes, not one script.
